units: Architecture document translates the Adaptive Inheritance Criterion into an executable evaluation pipeline.
Pipeline is Invariant -> Algorithm -> Telemetry -> Experimental Result.
Five functional layers have distinct responsibilities: PTVS detection, MRAT attribution, inheritance authority update, REE expansion gating, and RAHU experimental harness.
Data flow moves observation -> prediction -> environment transition -> residual -> PTVS -> MRAT -> noise/structural branch -> authority update -> future behavior evaluation.
PTVS operates on observable trajectories and is specified to report LBR, violations, and trajectory score.
PTVS is specified to detect mismatch but not decide correction.
MRAT maps residuals to N/S/M/R/G attribution components.
MRAT is intended to determine the lowest-cost explanation for failure and prevent blind updates.
Inheritance layer maintains mechanism authority, admissibility score, and historical performance.
REE determines whether representation expansion is justified rather than reacting automatically to failure.
REE specification requires bounded-search residual saturation and expected future value greater than representation cost.
RAHU evaluator executes benchmark environments and calculates final metrics.
Specified adaptive-agent interface includes predict, commit_mechanism, update, and get_authority_weights.
Specified telemetry includes LBR, C_pre, C_post, MRAT vector, structural distance, R_update, ARR, tau_authority, and ACS.
A valid structural update is specified to require D(M1,M2)>theta.
Structural distance is intended to distinguish genuine mechanism change from cosmetic wording or exception changes.
RAHU is required to be black-box compatible and not require chain-of-thought, hidden activations, or private representations.
Detection, attribution, and correction are explicitly separated into different layers.
Benchmark objective is minimum structural change required for future validity, not maximum change.
Successful adaptation is summarized as E* -> Phi_R(e_t) -> Delta W -> W_(t+1).
Architecture does not define a domain-general trajectory generator or admissibility-construction procedure.
Architecture does not identify how N/S/M/R/G attribution mass is causally estimated.
Architecture does not identify authority weights with intervention-derived future causal influence.
Architecture leaves estimators for residual compressibility, future value, representation cost, and approximate-equality thresholds open.
Architecture names possible structural-distance implementations but does not select or validate one.
Architecture describes a validation pathway but supplies no reported validation result.
